sections.title: Quick Answer
sections.content: The best Islamic lock screen app for iPhone is **QuranWall**. It is designed for the lock screen: it places an ayah on your Lock Screen wallpaper and Home Screen widget, in Uthmani Arabic or a translation. QuranWall is our app, so it is ranked first here; this is the honest case.

sections.text: Most lists of Islamic apps point you to a reader or a prayer-times app and call it done. But if your real goal is to *see* the Quran without opening anything, you need a different kind of tool. This guide ranks the **best Islamic lock screen app for iPhone**, starting with the one built for that job, then the apps worth keeping for reading, memorizing, and prayer times. Each is good at something. Other Quran widget apps exist too, so check the App Store listings and compare.

sections.label: phone checks a day
sections.description: Americans say they check their phones about 186 times a day, per Reviews.org's 2026 survey of about 1,000 US adults (self-reported). A verse on the lock screen turns those glances into small reminders.

sections.text: What makes a great Islamic lock screen app
Not every app labelled Islamic belongs on your lock screen. The **best Islamic lock screen app for iPhone** clears a short, strict bar:

items: **Lives on the lock screen.** A real widget or wallpaper, not a notification you swipe away.
**Easy to keep fresh.** Changing the ayah takes a few taps in the app, and the widget can show a new one every day if you turn on auto-rotate.
**Built for the surface.** Designed to sit right under the clock, not a reading-app screenshot.
**No ads.** Nothing competing with the verse for your attention.

sections.text: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.
The 5 best Islamic lock screen apps for iPhone, ranked
1. QuranWall — the lock-screen native (our pick)

**QuranWall** wins because it is built around one job: putting a Quran ayah on the surface you already see all day. It sets the ayah as your Lock Screen wallpaper and Home Screen widget, in Uthmani Arabic or in a translation, in your choice of 10 languages. You choose the background, font and colours — a preset or your own photo — and you can search all 114 surahs by surah, ayah or keyword. There are no ads, and it works offline.

New to it? Start with the [iPhone lock-screen setup guide](/blog/quran-verse-iphone-lock-screen), or pair it with a [Quiet Time Focus mode](/blog/quran-focus-mode-iphone) so your Quran lock screen appears around your prayer times.
2. Muslim Pro — best for prayer times and qibla

Muslim Pro is the long-standing all-in-one: accurate prayer times, qibla direction, adhan, and a Quran reader. If you want a single app for the daily prayer schedule, it's a strong choice. What it isn't is a lock-screen app. The Quran stays inside it, one tap away rather than already in front of you.
3. Quran.com and Quran Majeed — best for reading and tafsir

For sitting down to read, Quran.com (from the Quran Foundation) and Quran Majeed are excellent: clean Arabic, several translations, tafsir, and audio. They are reading tools, though. They are where you go to study, not what greets you when you lift your phone.
4. Tarteel — best for memorization
Tarteel uses AI to follow your recitation and support hifz, catching slips as you memorize. For that narrow, important job it's genuinely useful. It does nothing for your lock screen.
5. Athan by IslamicFinder — best for adhan reminders

Athan is built around prayer-time notifications and the adhan. If reminders to pray are your gap, it fills it well. But a prayer alert isn't a verse you read; it's a notification you act on and dismiss.

sections.content: Notice the pattern. Muslim Pro is for prayer times. Quran.com and Tarteel are for reading and memorizing. Athan is for the adhan. QuranWall is for the daily-exposure surface you check all day: the lock screen. Other Quran widget apps exist, so compare listings before you choose.

sections.text: Where this gets hard

You could skip the apps and just save a verse image as your wallpaper. Two things break it. First, a reading-app screenshot isn't designed for the lock screen, so the text lands under the clock, the margins are off, and it looks like a screenshot because it is one. Second, the habit dies by week two. Changing your wallpaper by hand is a small chore you'll quietly stop doing.

**QuranWall** removes both problems. It is designed for the lock-screen surface, so you are not screenshotting, cropping or exporting images into your Camera Roll. Changing the ayah takes a few taps inside QuranWall, and the widget can show a new ayah every day if you turn on auto-rotate.
How to set it up

items: Open it and choose your translation language, background, font and colours.
Put the ayah on your Lock Screen wallpaper and add the QuranWall widget to your Home Screen.
Optional: add a lock-screen widget from the lock-screen editor, or, on iOS 16 or later, link that Lock Screen to a Focus (touch and hold the Lock Screen, then tap Focus).
A new verse now meets you every time you check your phone.

sections.content: QuranWall lists iOS 15.0 or later. Apple added Lock Screen widgets and per-Focus lock screens in iOS 16, so for those parts of this guide, update in Settings > General > Software Update first if your iPhone is older.

sections.text: Frequently asked questions
Does it work on every iPhone?
QuranWall lists iOS 15.0 or later in the App Store. Lock Screen widgets and per-Focus lock screens arrived in iOS 16, so the Focus-mode steps in this guide need iOS 16 or later.

sections.title: The short version
sections.content: For reading, choose Quran.com. For prayer times, Muslim Pro. For memorizing, Tarteel. But for the **best Islamic lock screen app for iPhone** — a daily Quran ayah on the surface you already check — QuranWall is our pick.
